dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: When you reflect a point across the x-axis, which coordinate changes sign?
dialogue_stages.student_response: I think the x-coordinate flips because it's called reflection in the x-axis?
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Careful! Think of the x-axis as a flat mirror on the ground. A point hovering above the axis reflects to an identical position directly below it. Its horizontal position (x) stays unchanged; only its vertical elevation (y) flips sign: (x, y) -> (x, -y).

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: Find the reflection of Q(7, -9) in the y-axis, and state which quadrant the image point belongs to.
dialogue_stages.student_response: Reflection in the y-axis inverts the horizontal position, so (7, -9) becomes (-7, -9). Since both x and y are negative, it lies in Quadrant III.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Perfect! You accurately applied the transformation rule and identified the correct quadrant.

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: What happens if a point lies directly on the axis of reflection, such as (5, 0) reflected in the x-axis?
dialogue_stages.student_response: The y-coordinate is 0, and -0 is 0, so the point stays at (5, 0). Points on the reflection line are invariant.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Brilliant! Points lying on the line of reflection are fixed points of the isometry.
